headline: Indian Markets Under Pressure as Nifty Hits 52-Week Low Following RBI Rate Hike and IT Sector Concerns

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: The RBI hiked interest rates for the first time in nearly four years to address inflation concerns.
Major Indian IT firms face suspension from the US green card (PERM) programme, impacting sentiment.
Rising crude oil prices and high US bond yields are weighing heavily on global and domestic markets.
Concerns over a potential steep hike in rice prices and eroding housing demand due to high mortgage rates.
whatHappening: Nifty 50 has breached the 22,600 level and hit a fresh 52-week low following a sharp sell-off.
The Sensex plummeted over 1,000 points in a single session, snapping previous winning runs.
Metal and consumer durable stocks, including Hindalco and Titan, have emerged as top laggards.
US tech stocks are dragging global indices lower amid reports of revenue declines at major AI firms.
summary: Indian markets are facing significant volatility with the Nifty hitting a 52-week low after the RBI's first rate hike in nearly four years. The IT sector is under pressure following reports of a US green card programme suspension for major firms like TCS and Infosys. Global cues remain weak due to rising crude prices and high US mortgage rates affecting investor confidence.
